info.description:
GitHub · crates.io

Python bindings for the tokie Rust tokenizer. The `tokie` Python package is 0.3.0 and wraps the Rust `tokie` 0.2.0 crate. `encode`, `encode_plus`, and `batch` release the GIL and return NumPy arrays. There is no `Encoding` object and no `.ids` attribute; use `.tolist()` only to print or assert. `decode` and `decode_bytes` take the array returned by `encode`, `encode_plus`, or a slice of `batch`'s flat `uint32` ids. Pass it directly; do not call `.tolist()` first. The array must be one-dimensional, native-endian, C-contiguous, and aligned `uint32`. Lists, tuples, and arrays of another dtype are rejected; 0.2.0 also accepted lists. ## Installation ```bash pip install -U tokie ``` Pin a floor with `pip install "tokie>=0.3.0"` when a resolver needs one. ## Quick start ```python import tokie tokenizer = tokie.Tokenizer.from_pretrained("openai-community/gpt2") # from_json(path) and from_file(path) are aliases for open(path). ids = tokenizer.encode("Hello world") # uint32 array, template off print(ids.tolist()) print(tokenizer.decode(ids)) print(tokenizer.decode_bytes(ids)) # raw bytes # The single-sequence template. GPT-2 has none, so this matches encode. print(tokenizer.encode_plus("Hello world").tolist()) flat, ends = tokenizer.batch(["Hello world", "a12b"]) # ends are cumulative print(tokenizer.count_tokens("Hello world")) # template off print(tokenizer.count_tokens_batch(["Hello world", "a12b"])) print(tokenizer.vocab_size) # highest id + 1 print(tokenizer.pad_token_id) # [PAD] then print(tokenizer.num_special_tokens_to_add(is_pair=False)) tokenizer.save("gpt2.tokie") ``` `encode` leaves the template off. `encode_plus` applies it and accepts `pair`, `truncate`, and `pad`; truncation is from the right, longest sequence first, and padding is fixed on the right. One `max_len` covers both and counts the template ids. `from_pretrained` opens exactly one `.tokie` file from the repo, whatever its name. A repo with no `.tokie` file is parsed from `tokenizer.json`; several `.tokie` files is an error. There is no runtime `.tkz` fallback: a genuine legacy `TOKI` image is refused by magic, not by extension, while a JSON file merely named `.tkz` is parsed as JSON. `open` reads either file from disk by its magic, `from_json(path)` and `from_file(path)` are path aliases for `open`, and `json(text)` parses JSON text. `decode` returns `str` (lossy only where needed). `decode_bytes` returns raw bytes. Both take the `uint32` array as their first argument and keep specials by default; `skip=True` omits them. For ids built by hand, convert explicitly: `numpy.asarray(values, dtype=numpy.uint32)`. That is your conversion, not an API fallback. For an arbitrary existing array use `numpy.array(values, dtype=numpy.uint32, copy=True, order="C")`; `numpy.ascontiguousarray` does not fix an already C-contiguous but misaligned buffer. `get_vocab()` returns raw token strings and may have fewer entries than `vocab_size`. ## Benchmark `bench.py` times `Tokenizer.encode` on one file against the `tokie bench` command, which is the Rust path. ## License MIT OR Apache-2.0
